messages.content: You design amateur rockets that fly on certified commercial motors. Work through the design, check it with the tools, and give the final design as JSON inside <design> tags. Only report results the tools returned.
About 450 m, land within 800 m of the pad in 5 m/s wind, single chute.

messages.reasoning_content:
1. Understand: About 450 m means 428 to 473 m. One chute. It has to land within 800 m of the pad, and the wind is 5 m/s, so that wind goes on every run. Rail, site, and landing speed are not stated: 1.5 m, sea level, and 6 m/s. Drift is the horizontal miss, not the touchdown speed. A 450 m fall at 5 m/s takes 450 / 5 = 90 s, and 90 * 5 = 450 m of drift if the wind just carried it the whole way, so 800 m is roomy if the chute is not huge.
2. Feasibility: A D has been short of 450 m once it is stable. An E is the class to try. The wind is strong enough that an overstable fin set will weathercock and walk off downrange.

2. Feasibility: Estes E12 is class E, 27.1 N*s, 11.2 N, 2.41 s, 24 mm by 0.095 m, 0.0599 kg, delays 0, 4, 6, and 8 s. The E16 is 33.6 N*s in a 29 mm case and heavier, 0.082 kg. The D12 is 16.8 N*s, light for 450 m once the fins are honest. I will fly the E12. On a guessed 0.16 kg rocket, thrust-to-weight is 11.2 / (0.16 * 9.81) = 7.1. An 8 s delay ejects at 2.41 + 8 = 10.4 s.
3. Size: For 0.16 kg at 5 m/s the chute is 2 * 0.16 * 9.81 / (1.225 * 0.8 * 5^2) = 0.13 m^2, diameter sqrt(4 * 0.13 / 3.1416) = 0.41 m. I will use 0.42 m so the landing stays near 5 m/s and the hang time stays short in 5 m/s of wind. A little nose mass, 0.012 kg, keeps the E from sitting on the tail.
4. Draft: Cardboard ogive 0.12 m on a 0.50 m cardboard tube, outer diameter 0.038 m, wall 1 mm. E12 with an 8 s delay, chute at ejection. Three birch fins, root 0.09 m, tip 0.04 m, span 0.06 m, sweep 0.04 m, 3 mm. Wind 5 m/s.

4. Check: The simulator gives 438.8 m, inside 5% of 450 m. Drift is 434 m, inside 800 m. Landing 4.3 m/s, and it reached the ground. Rail exit 20.6 m/s and thrust-to-weight 7.0 pass. The rail margin is 0.58 cal, and the burn minimum is 0.58 cal, so it is still short of 1 cal in 5 m/s of wind. Mass 0.163 kg. Chute at 10.4 s, after the 8.79 s apogee.
5. Fix: 0.58 cal is the miss. Altitude and drift are already good, so I am not growing the fins. I am adding 0.010 kg at 0.03 m, on top of the 0.012 kg already there, to move the CG forward with less drag than a bigger fin. Wind stays 5 m/s.

4. Check: The simulator gives 427.7 m, still within 5% of 450 m. Drift is 393 m, inside 800 m. Margin is 1.02 cal at the rail and through the burn. Rail exit 20.6 m/s, thrust-to-weight 6.6, landing 4.5 m/s, chute at 10.4 s, and it reached the ground. Mass 0.173 kg.
5. Fix: 427.7 m, 393 m of drift, and 1.02 cal all clear, so I am leaving the nose weight where it is.
6. Uncertainty: 427.7 m and 1.02 cal are both close to the line. Another 5 g in the nose, or a fin that is a little smaller, could drop one of them under. Five m/s of wind is doing real work: the drift is 393 m, and a longer hang time would use up the 800 m budget. The 8 s delay opens at 10.4 s, after the 8.85 s apogee. Cd 0.8 is what makes 4.5 m/s.
messages.content:
Estes E12-8, single chute, flown in 5 m/s wind.
Apogee is 427.7 m, within 5% of 450 m, and drift is 393 m, inside 800 m.
Margin 1.02 cal, landing 4.5 m/s, and it reached the ground.
